'''The Linnik class''' <math>I_0</math> is one of the central concepts in the arithmetic of [[Probability distribution|probability distributions]]. Following [[Yuri Linnik|Yuri Vladimirovich Linnik]], denote by <math>I_0</math> the class of distributions that have no indecomposable divisors.
Examples of distributions belonging to the class <math>I_0</math> include [[Normal distribution|normal distributions]] ([[Cramér's decomposition theorem]]), [[Poisson distribution|Poisson distributions]] ([[Raikov's theorem]]), as well as their convolutions ([[Linnik's theorem on the decomposition of the convolution of a normal and a Poisson distribution|Linnik's theorem]]).

== Properties distributions of the Linnik class==

Let <math>\mu \in I_0</math>. Then, according to [[Khinchin's theorem|Khinchin's second theorem]], the distribution <math>\mu</math> is [[Infinitely divisible distribution|infinitely divisible]]. Hence, by the Lévy formula, its characteristic function can be represented in the form
<div class="center"> <math>\hat\mu(s)=\exp\left\{i\beta s - \sigma s^2 + \int\limits_{\mathbb{R}\backslash \{0\}} \left(e^{ixs} - 1 - {ixs \over 1 +x^2}\right)dF(x)\right\}, \quad\quad\quad (1)</math> </div>
where <math>\beta\in \mathbb{R}</math>, <math>\sigma \ge 0</math>, and   <math>F</math> is a Borel measure on <math>\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}</math> satisfying the condition
<math>\int_{\mathbb{R}\backslash \{0\}} {x^2\over {1+x^2}}dF(x)<\infty.</math> 
The measure <math>F</math> is called the Lévy spectral measure of the infinitely divisible distribution <math>\mu</math>.
The central problem in the arithmetic of probability distributions is to determine conditions on <math>\sigma</math> and <math>F</math> that are necessary and sufficient for an infinitely divisible distribution <math>\mu</math> to belong to the class <math>I_0</math>.

Denote by <math>\mathfrak{L}</math> the class of infinitely divisible distributions <math>\mu</math> having the property that the Lévy spectral measure <math>F</math> in (1) is discrete and concentrated on a set of the form
<div class="center">
<math>
\{\mu_{k1}\}_{k=-\infty}^\infty \cup \{\mu_{k2}\}_{k=-\infty}^\infty,
</math>
</div>
where <math>\mu_{k1}>0</math>, <math>\mu_{k2}<0</math>, and the numbers <math>\mu_{k+1, r}/\mu_{k, r}</math>, <math>r=1, 2</math>, <math>k=0, \pm 1, \pm 2, \dots</math>, are natural numbers different from 1. 

The following remarkable theorem is due to Yu. V. Linnik.

''Theorem 1''<ref name="Linnik1958">Linnik, Yu. V. General theorems on the decomposition of infinitely divisible laws. I // Theory of Probability and Its Applications. — 1958. — Vol. 3, No. 1. — P. 3–40</ref>. Let <math>\mu</math> be an infinitely divisible distribution and suppose that in formula (1), <math>\sigma>0</math>. If <math>\mu\in I_0</math>, then <math>\mu\in \mathfrak{L}</math>.

Note that there exist distributions belonging to the class <math>\mathfrak{L}</math> but not to <math>I_0</math>. A corresponding example was constructed in <ref name="GoldbergOstrovsky1967">Goldberg, A. A.; Ostrovskii, I. V. Application of W. K. Hayman's theorem to a problem in the theory of decomposition of probability laws // Ukrainian Mathematical Journal. — 1967. — Vol. 19, No. 3. — P. 104–106.</ref>. On the other hand, under the additional assumption of rapid decay of the quantity <math>\int_{|x|> y} dF (x) </math> as <math>y \rightarrow\infty</math>, membership in the class <math>\mathfrak{L}</math> implies membership in the class <math>I_0</math><ref name="LinnikOstrovsky1972">Linnik, Yu. V.; Ostrovskii, I. V. Decomposition of Random Variables and Vectors. — Moscow: Nauka, 1972</ref>.

We present two results concerning membership in the class <math>I_0</math> of a generalized Poisson distribution, i.e., an infinitely divisible distribution <math>\mu</math> such that in (1), <math>\sigma=0</math> and the Lévy spectral measure <math>F</math> is finite.

''Theorem 2''<ref name="Ostrovsky1965">Ostrovskii, I. V. On decompositions of infinitely divisible laws without a Gaussian component // Doklady Akademii Nauk SSSR. — 1965. — Vol. 161, No. 1. — P. 48–51.</ref>. Suppose that in (1), <math>\sigma=0</math>, the Lévy spectral measure <math>F</math> is finite and concentrated on the interval <math>(a, b)</math>, where <math>0<a<b\le 2a</math>. Then <math>\mu\in I_0</math>.

''Theorem 3''<ref name="Cuppens1971">Cuppens, R. Ensembles indépendants et décomposition des fonctions caractéristiques // C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris, Série A-B. — 1971. — Vol. 272. — P. A1464–A1466</ref>. Suppose that in (1), <math>\sigma=0</math>, the Lévy spectral measure <math>F</math> is finite and concentrated on a set of independent points. Then <math>\mu\in I_0</math>.

The following two theorems describe the properties of the class  <math>I_0</math> as a subclass of the class of all infinitely divisible distributions.

''Theorem 4''<ref name="Ostrovsky1970">Ostrovskii, I. V. On certain classes of infinitely divisible laws // Izvestiya Akademii Nauk SSSR, Seriya Matematicheskaya. — 1970. — Vol. 34, No. 4. — P. 923–944</ref>. The class <math>I_0</math> is dense (in the weak topology) in the class of all infinitely divisible distributions.

''Theorem 5''<ref name="Ostrovsky1965"/>. Any infinitely divisible distribution can be represented as a finite or countable convolution of distributions belonging to the class <math>I_0</math>.
